answer: Every agent must answer echo probes sent by randomly chosen verifiers at dawn and dusk; the round-trip latencies triangulate where it really runs. Hundreds of sybils packed on one rented server return the same latency fingerprint, so the registry shades that cluster umber on its map and merges it into one identity with one reward share. Faking distinct locations means renting real machines across many regions, which costs more than the farm could skim.
